_doc: Cleanup preset, the engine behind /code-cleanup. Each lens is one cleanup concern, so a run uses all of them. Not benchmarked: the lenses are the /code-cleanup mandates as they shipped before /fanout.
task: Find cleanup work in this codebase within your concern only, and propose each change with the evidence that makes it safe. Do not report bugs or style outside your concern.
recon_extra: Read the lint and type config (tsconfig, ESLint, ruff.toml, clippy.toml, .editorconfig) and the test layout.
Check which cleanup tools are installed and actually run: knip, ts-prune, madge, depcheck, vulture, deadcode, pydeps, cargo machete, cargo udeps. Note the working ones; forks use only those.
report_line: {"file": "...", "line": <n>, "sites": ["path:line", ...every site, not a sample], "title": "<short>", "evidence": "<the grep output, AST match or tool output that proves it>", "change": "<concrete enough to apply without re-investigating; a diff when short>", "confidence": "high|medium|low", "risk": "<what could break: dynamic wiring, reflection, public API, generated code>", "conflicts": "<other concerns this change touches, or empty>"}
keep_if: the evidence still holds when you re-check it in the code.

lenses.brief: Deduplicate. Find repeated logic across the codebase. Propose DRY only where it cuts real complexity, never abstraction for its own sake; leave three-line repetition alone.
Consolidate types. Find type definitions duplicated across files or packages. Propose one source of truth for each shared shape and list every import that must change.

Dead code. Run the cleanup tools the recon confirmed work. Find unreferenced exports, files and dependencies. Grep the full tree, tests, configs and dynamic imports included, before calling anything dead.
Circular dependencies. Run madge, pydeps or the equivalent. For each cycle, propose the break: invert a dependency or extract the shared piece. Never propose masking it with lazy imports.
Weak types. Find every any, unknown, object, {}, Python Any, Go interface{} and Rust Box<dyn Any>. Read the call sites and upstream types, and propose the real type for each.

Defensive programming. Find every try/catch and equivalent. Keep only those handling real external input, documented failure modes, or boundaries the caller cannot cross. Propose removing empty catches, silent fallbacks and speculative guards.
Legacy paths. Find deprecated code, compatibility shims, fallback branches, TODO-remove-after-X notes that outlived X, and feature flags long since defaulted. Propose the single canonical path.

AI slop. Find narration comments, 'replaced old Y with new Z' notes, commented-out code, comments that restate the code, and stub scaffolds. Keep comments that explain why, constraints or non-obvious invariants; propose rewrites of those for a new reader, with no references to prior versions.
